recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-32506 unless a later work-group decision changes Procedure.performer semantics.
issue_request: FHIR-32506 asked Patient Care to fix Procedure.performer's definition and short display because the old wording implied performers were only people, while Procedure.performer.actor can be Device, Organization, and other non-person actors. The final request was to use "Who performed the procedure and what they did" and "Indicates who or what performed the procedure and how they were involved."
initial_application: Commit 85f9053b69a48a8556aad22b881efe9997508eef, identified in the Jira comments as GH#85f9053, applied J#32506 by changing source/procedure/structuredefinition-Procedure.xml from "The people who performed the procedure" and "Limited to \"real\" people rather than equipment." to the requested who-or-what wording. Current git blame still attributes the Procedure.performer short and definition lines to that commit.
additional_context: Procedure is listed as an active resource and marked approved in source/fhir.ini, so the inspected StructureDefinition is in current build scope. The procedure-event-mapping-exceptions.xml file records only the expected short-text divergence from the Event pattern. Patient Care minutes from 2023-03-02 reference FHIR-32506, matching the Jira vote date. The same implementation commit also mentions FHIR-32508, but that separate issue concerns Procedure.location and was not decided here.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch. The current build-scope Procedure source already carries the requested short and definition, so another source edit would be redundant.

related_jiras.note: Mentioned in the same implementation commit and PC minutes, but it concerns Procedure.location rather than the Procedure.performer wording audited for FHIR-32506.
